correctness.rationale: The next accepted edge is uniform among edges of the current free-vertex graph: all those edges have survived in the unexplored order and eligibility can only be lost. The three transition weights are ab, ac, bc. For a fixed free C vertex, the chance of matching on the next acceptance is 1/(ab/(a+b)+c) >= 1/(s+r), s=min(a,b). Before s first drops below h the chain must traverse every level from n to h, so conditioning at the first departure attempt at each level gives the telescoping survival bound (h+r-1)/(n+r). Union over r vertices. Pre-sample independent uniforms for the successive C matches and use the same uniforms for fair coins, whether or not each uniform ends up being used. The endpoint probability differs from 1/2 by at most r/(4h) whenever s>=h because |a-b|<=r. The probability of any early mismatch is at most r^2/(4h). On the good event, c=0 and A-B matches exhaust the smaller part, leaving the absolute coin imbalance. This proves the stated TV bound for every admissible integer h including h=n and covers small n by the same inequality, even when vacuous. h near sqrt(nr) gives the growing-r estimate; the binomial CLT and TV contraction under scaling transfer the half-normal limit. The r=2 graph admits a perfect matching by using one third-part vertex with each principal part and matching the remaining principal vertices. Read the frozen verification note and script: exact count-state and labeled-state recurrences, three exhaustive order tests, and finite rational inequalities; reported counts were not independently replayed and are not required for the analytic argument.

value.rationale: The law isolates a nonvanishing jamming defect in a natural dense, perfectly matchable (for r=2) perturbation of a balanced graph. It predicts finite-size fluctuations and quantifies convergence that vacancy fractions and parity alone cannot see. This is substantive mathematical value of the theorem as a result, not originality credit for a second formulation or for changes in constants.
